Hakon.narrative: I was raised among Brandholm's timber and learned to make a roof hold through a hard winter. Rose and I built our home here at Oathstone, where the land belongs to neither town and our children belong to both. I want the berry bushes left standing, and I have little patience for hunters who treat this place as empty ground.
goals: Keep the hunters from trampling Oathstone's bushes
Make sure my family has what it needs for winter
Keep ties with my parents without letting Brandholm decide how we live
Hakon.mood: Watchful and irritated, softened by the noise of my children.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She knows when I am angry before I say a word, and she steadies me.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He notices every slight; I wish the other children would let him simply be a boy.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows Rose around and brings the whole house to a halt when she laughs.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is still small enough to sleep against my chest through the night.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me to make things that last, even if he does not always understand my choices.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She sends berries and questions in equal measure; I miss having her close.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She speaks plainly and does not ask me to choose a town before she listens.

relations.name: Kjell
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: His hunting has crushed the bushes, and I have not forgotten it.

relations.name: Brann
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He talks as if the middle lands are his to take.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: Rose's brother has tended people on both sides; I value that kind of work.

memories.gist: When I left Brandholm to make a home with Rose, the gossip followed us farther than the road did. We planted anyway.
The Oath renewal brought traders and witnesses to the stone; I watched people who distrusted each other still make room to speak.
I found fresh tracks through the berry ring after Brann's hunters had crossed. Some bushes were crushed flat.
The children came one by one, and each time Rose made our small home feel bigger than either town's judgment.

stances.why: We depend on one another more than either town likes to admit.
A planted bush takes years to bear; a careless hunter can ruin it in a moment.
My family is proof that neither town can claim every useful thing or every person.

Rose.narrative: I grew up where the southern water feeds the nets, and I still miss the sound of it when the hills go quiet. Here I tend people and plants, and I make our home warm with whatever food and medicine the land gives us. Some people have never forgiven me for choosing Hakon, but I have not regretted choosing him.
values: Care that is useful, not showy
A home where children are safe
goals: Help the berry bushes and plantings thrive
Keep my family connected to Saltreach without letting old grief rule us
Be ready to tend anyone who comes to our door hurt or ill
Rose.mood: Steady and affectionate, with a sore place where old judgments land.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He works hard for us, though anger can make him forget how much I hear.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: son
relations.note: He tries to look unbothered when children tease him, and I know better.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She asks questions with her whole face and expects an answer.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Her little hand closes around my finger as if it could keep me there.

relations.name: Fen
relations.label: brother
relations.note: We were children together in Saltreach; I trust his hands and his judgment.

relations.name: Ilse
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: She has not forgiven my marriage, and her grief has reasons I cannot erase.

relations.name: Tamsin
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She treats me as a person, not as a tale the towns tell about a marriage.

relations.name: Aud
relations.label: keeper
relations.note: She has made room for us at the stone without asking us to explain ourselves.

relations.name: Halvard
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He is quieter than Hakon, but his welcome has mattered to me.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She fusses over the children and asks after my plants as if they are kin.

relations.name: Oriel
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Fen's partner knows the work of tending people and food; I like her, though we mostly meet through him.

memories.gist: When I first made a home with Hakon, some Saltreach faces went cool toward me. I held on to the people who still came to visit.
I helped tend the berry bushes beside the stone and learned which patches hold damp after the rain.
A child came to me sick and frightened, and by morning the fever had eased. Their mother stayed until the fire went low.
The children have grown up hearing both towns named as theirs and neither as fully theirs. I have tried to make our own doorway feel certain.

stances.why: They did not choose the quarrels that came before them.
Hurt and sickness do not ask which town a person belongs to.
Plants and people both need tending before they can give anything back.

Wynn.narrative: I live by the stone with my mother, father, and sisters. Some children call me half this and half that, like it is a joke, but I know the paths and the berry bushes better than they do. I like being with Kit, and I like fires when someone tells a good story.
values: Being brave when people tease me
goals: Have children from both towns play with me without making it a contest
Help look after Asa and Linnet
See more of the paths around the stone
Wynn.mood: Curious, with a little hurt tucked under my boldness.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: He can build things from sticks and boards, and he gets cross when bushes are crushed.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She can tell when I am pretending not to care.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She wants to copy everything I do, even when I tell her not to.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: sister
relations.note: I like making her smile when she is cross.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: Kit collects shells and odd stones, and always has something to show me.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She brings stories and berries when she visits, and I wish she came more often.

memories.gist: A child from one of the towns called me neither one nor the other. I went back to the berry bushes instead of answering.
Kit and I compared stones by the planted ring and argued over which one looked most like a fish.

Asa.narrative: I live near the big grey stone with Mama and Papa. Wynn is my brother and Linnet is my baby sister. I like berries and sitting close when the fire is warm.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: Papa makes things and lets me watch.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Mama always knows where I am.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: brother
relations.note: I like following him, even when he says I am too small.

relations.name: Linnet
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is little and I like making her laugh.

relations.name: Kit
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: Kit has funny stones to show me.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Grandmother Astrid gives me berries and makes me feel welcome when I visit.

memories.gist: I picked a berry and got juice all over my fingers. Mama laughed and wiped them clean.

Linnet.narrative: Warm arms. A fire flickers and makes the room bright. Voices come close, and I sleep against Mama.

relations.name: Hakon
relations.label: father
relations.note: His arms are broad and his voice rumbles.

relations.name: Rose
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Her warmth and smell are familiar.

relations.name: Wynn
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He makes noises near me and sometimes I smile.

relations.name: Asa
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is close and lively.

relations.name: Astrid
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Her voice and gentle hands feel familiar when she visits.
